$comment: Sample Quiver catalog for offline smoke tests. NOT for production Wox — replace with your own aliases. Field contract and placeholders documented in ~/.dotfiles/docs/wox/README.md §3.

commands.description: Echo the query back — the `{query}` placeholder is replaced verbatim (no shell escaping).

Primary outbound IPv4 (Linux): the `src` address of the default route. Enter copies it. `capture: true` runs at query time so the result lands on the clipboard via Wox's `copy-to-clipboard` action. (No `awk '{print $N}'` here — the plugin's `$N` substitution blanks a bare `$N` before bash ever sees it; see §3.1 for the `${N}` spelling.)
Primary outbound IPv4 (Windows PowerShell). The same capture contract on the other interpreter; `interpreter: powershell` is only honored on Windows builds.
Open `$HOME/workspace` in Explorer; `silent: true` makes Wox hide immediately after Enter, leaving the action running detached.
`qv k get pods -o wide` — `kubectl` receives all arguments verbatim via `$@`. Custom-Commands-style placeholders, joined by one space.

Uppercase the first positional: `qv upper hello` prints HELLO. The inner `"${1}"` (braced) escapes the plugin's outer `$N` substitution and reaches the inner `sh`; the trailing `"$1"` is substituted by the plugin at query time and handed to that inner shell as its first positional.
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. A minimal `capture: true` example: the entry's stdout is the clipboard payload.
